text: Drink a full glass of water.
whyItMatters: After a night without drinking it's the easiest first win. In a small trial, people who normally drank little felt less tired and less muddled when they drank more.
variations: Drink it before you look at your phone.
Drink it standing at the window.
Fill a bottle to carry with you today.

text: Step outside or open a window for two minutes and look at the sky.
whyItMatters: Daylight is what sets your body clock. In two small camping studies, a week of natural light moved people's internal clocks about two hours earlier.
variations: Walk to the gate and back.

text: Climb one flight of stairs briskly, twice.
whyItMatters: In a six-week trial, three short bursts of stair climbing a day improved fitness in inactive adults. The gain was small, but it came from a few minutes a day.
variations: Take the stairs instead of the lift today.

text: Ten slow squats with a chair behind you.
whyItMatters: The WHO recommends muscle-strengthening work at least twice a week. Ten squats is a start you can do in your pyjamas.
variations: Squat until you touch the chair.

text: Ten push-ups against a wall or kitchen counter.
whyItMatters: The same WHO guideline, upper body this time.
variations: Ten off the edge of the bed.

text: Stand on one leg for 30 seconds, then the other.
whyItMatters: In a study of 1,702 adults aged 51 to 75, those who couldn't stand on one leg for 10 seconds were more likely to die within seven years. It's an association, not proof that practising helps, but balance is worth keeping.
variations: Keep your eyes on a fixed point.
Try it while brushing your teeth.
safety: Stand next to a wall or something steady.

text: End your shower with 30 seconds of cold water.
whyItMatters: In a trial with 3,018 adults, people who finished with a cold shower took 29% fewer sick days off work, though they didn't fall ill less often.
variations: Cold water on your face and wrists.
safety: Skip this one if you have a heart condition.

text: Add one piece of fruit to your breakfast.
whyItMatters: A review of 95 studies found that every extra 200 g of fruit and vegetables a day went with a 10% lower risk of early death.
variations: A banana on the way out.
A handful of whatever fruit is in season.

text: Six slow breaths: in for five seconds, out for five.
whyItMatters: A systematic review found slow breathing (under ten breaths a minute) linked to calmer heart rhythms and less anxiety.

text: Reach up, lean side to side, then reach for your toes. One minute.
whyItMatters: A review of stretching studies found it improves range of movement for a short while afterwards. Good for stiff mornings; it won't prevent injuries on its own.

text: March on the spot, dance, or walk around for two minutes.
whyItMatters: The WHO guideline says any amount of movement beats none.
variations: Walk while you brush your teeth.

text: Do your first task of the day standing up.
whyItMatters: The WHO advises everyone to cut down time spent sitting. The guideline doesn't set a number, so small breaks count.

text: Send a short thank-you message to someone.
whyItMatters: People who wrote thank-you notes expected them to feel awkward. The people who received them were much happier than the writers predicted.
variations: A family member who helped this week.

text: Breathe in twice through your nose, then out slowly through your mouth. Five rounds.
whyItMatters: In a month-long trial, five minutes a day of this cyclic sighing improved mood more than mindfulness meditation did. One minute is a shorter version of what was tested.
variations: Make each exhale a little longer.

text: Think of something you're hard on yourself about. Write one line to yourself the way you'd write to a friend.
whyItMatters: In four experiments, people who were kind to themselves after a mistake were more motivated to improve, not less.
variations: About something you're nervous about today.

text: Decide one kind thing you'll do for someone today.
whyItMatters: A review of 27 studies found acts of kindness lift the giver's wellbeing. The effect is small but consistent.

text: Sit and notice your breathing for one minute.
whyItMatters: A review of mindfulness research links it to better wellbeing and less emotional reactivity.
variations: Notice where you feel the breath.

text: Stop and notice three sounds you can hear right now.
whyItMatters: Paying attention to the present without judging it is the core of mindfulness, which a review links to better wellbeing.

text: Write for two minutes about something on your mind. No editing.
whyItMatters: Across a decade of experiments, writing about emotional experiences was linked to fewer doctor visits and better health.

text: Write the single most important task for today.
whyItMatters: 35 years of goal-setting research shows that specific, clear goals lead to better performance than "do your best".
variations: The one that makes everything else easier.

text: Write one "If ___ happens, I will ___" for a problem you expect today.
whyItMatters: A review of 94 tests found that if-then plans help people follow through on goals. Later, stricter analyses found a smaller effect, but it held.
variations: If I feel like skipping the gym...

text: Pick the exact time and place you'll do your hardest task.
whyItMatters: Deciding when and where in advance makes starting easier, according to the same review of if-then plans.

text: List every unfinished thing on your mind for two minutes, then write the next step for one.
whyItMatters: In a set of experiments, making a plan for an unfinished task stopped it from distracting people, even before they did it.

text: Write three things you remember from something you read or learned yesterday.
whyItMatters: Students who tested themselves remembered much more a week later than students who reread the material.

text: Learn five words in a language you want, then test yourself without looking.
whyItMatters: Testing yourself and spacing practice out are two of the best-supported findings on memory.

text: Look back at notes from three days ago and quiz yourself on them.
whyItMatters: A review of 317 experiments found that spreading study out over time beats cramming.

text: Explain something you're learning out loud in 30 seconds, as if to a friend.
whyItMatters: In experiments, people who explained material out loud understood it better than people who only prepared.

text: Do one task for ten minutes before you open messages.
whyItMatters: Lab experiments show that switching between tasks costs time, and more so for complex tasks.

text: Read two pages of a book.
whyItMatters: In a study of 3,635 older adults, book readers lived longer than non-readers over 12 years. It's an association, but reading books, not news, made the difference.

text: Write one specific goal for this week that you could measure.
whyItMatters: Goal-setting research shows specific goals beat vague ones.
variations: A thing to finish by Friday.

text: Split today's main task into three steps, and write the very first physical action (open the file, call the number).
whyItMatters: Clear sub-goals make progress visible, and a concrete first step removes the "where do I start" delay.

text: Walk for two minutes, then write down one idea about anything.
whyItMatters: In four experiments, people came up with more creative ideas while walking and shortly after than while sitting.
variations: Think about a problem while you walk.

text: List five unusual uses for an everyday object near you.
whyItMatters: A review of 70 studies found that creativity training works, especially exercises that build thinking skills like this one.

text: Doodle anything for one minute.
whyItMatters: In a small experiment, people who doodled while listening to a dull message remembered 29% more of it.

text: Take a photo of something that caught your eye this morning.
whyItMatters: Across nine experiments, taking photos made people enjoy positive experiences more by making them pay closer attention.

text: Spend a minute looking at something big: the sky, a tree, the city.
whyItMatters: In an eight-week trial, older adults who looked for awe on short walks reported more joy and less daily distress.
variations: The tallest thing you can see.

text: Write a story in exactly six words.
whyItMatters: In a 13-day diary study of 658 young adults, days with more creative activity were followed by days with better mood.

text: Play one upbeat song and actively try to feel better while it plays.
whyItMatters: In two experiments, upbeat music lifted mood only for people who were deliberately trying to feel happier.

text: Write three lines without stopping or correcting.
whyItMatters: Research on expressive writing found benefits from writing freely; this is the short, playful version.

text: Pick two objects you can see and invent a product that combines them.
whyItMatters: Combining ideas is one of the thinking skills that a review of creativity training found most effective.

text: Write one "what if" question about your work or your day.
whyItMatters: Questioning assumptions is a creative skill that training can improve, according to the same review.
variations: What if it took half the time?
What if I did the opposite?
